newsitem.title: UK: Stg seen firing on all cylinders into next week.
newsitem.headline: Stg seen firing on all cylinders into next week.

text.p: The pound is expected to run full steam into next week, fuelled by interest rate rise speculation ahead of the monthly meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
Many traders expect the pound to eclipse its recent four-year highs against the mark and the dollar in the run-up.

Evidence of buoyant economic growth, the engine of sterling's 17 percent rally against the mark in the past five months, was reinforced on Wednesday by bumper results from electrical goods retailer Dixons Group Plc.
The company boosted first-half profits in the six months to November by 53 percent. Chairman Sir Stanley Kalms said Christmas trading was "highly satisfactory".

Official figures from the Bank of England released on Monday showed strong cash demand in December and pointed to a late buying spree ahead of Christmas. Comments late on Tuesday by Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies also helped to buoy the pound, traders said. Davies said he saw a need for a small rate rise soon in order to meet the government's inflation target. The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) distributive trades survey, due for release on Friday, will be closely eyed as the first formal indication of consumer spending in December and the post-Christmas sales period.

"A strong CBI survey will clearly increase speculation for a rate increase," said Edmund Nonis, UK economist at Nikko Europe. Nonis added, however, that the market might be getting a bit ahead of itself in terms of rates. "A February rate hike looks like the better bet, and sterling might be capped by failure to raise rates next week." The pound traded at 2.6560 marks at 1018 GMT, up from 2.6485/90 in late European trading on Tuesday. It hit a 52-month high at 2.6615 on Monday. Against the dollar, sterling traded at $1.6930 from $1.6945. It reached its highest level since October 1992 at $1.7163 on December 31. On a trade-weighted basis, the pound stood at a four-year high of 96.3, up from 96.1 at the close on Tuesday. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom +44 171 542 7792
